purpose: The application frame: a sticky top bar, a collapsible sidebar, and a content area that scrolls independently of both. It owns layout and chrome; the consumer owns every nav row, the brand, the footer and the page.

useInstead.when: you only need a page's inner layout
useInstead.use: Stack or Grid — is there navigation chrome around it, or just content?

useInstead.when: the surface is a dialog, drawer or panel
useInstead.use: your own container — AppShell is the whole viewport and assumes it

decision.authority: This guard is the authority for AppShell decisions in this package. Where it is silent, say so rather than borrowing a rule from another design system.
decision.beforeTheRules: AppShell renders NO navigation rows of its own. Everything in the sidebar body comes from `navItems`. If you find yourself hardcoding a nav row inside the shell, you are editing the wrong layer.

rules.if: you are building the top-level route of an application
rules.then: render exactly one AppShell, at the root, wrapping all page content
rules.because: it sizes itself to the viewport with 100vh and owns the only scroll container; two nested shells give you two scrollbars and a doubled top bar

rules.then: pass it as `navItems` data and let the shell render it
rules.because: depth, active state, the 3-level cap and the collapsed rail are all derived from the tree; hand-written rows get none of them
the shell renders `<As href={...}>` and imports no router; without this every nav click does a full page load

rules.if: you want the notifications bell or the profile avatar
rules.then: pass `notifications` and `profile`; do NOT compose NotificationsMenu or ProfileMenu into topNavActions
rules.because: the shell mounts them at the right edge in a fixed order so users moving between applications find them in the same place; composing them yourself puts them wherever your JSX happens to place them

rules.if: you need any other top-bar control
rules.because: it renders to the LEFT of the bell and avatar, so adding a control never shifts the two fixed ones
the content slot takes the slack between the toggle and the actions, so a long trail shrinks rather than pushing the actions off the bar

rules.if: you are choosing a collapse mode
rules.then: leave `collapsible` at 'icon' unless the rail's glyphs are meaningless alone
rules.because: 'icon' keeps navigation reachable at 56px; 'offcanvas' removes it entirely and costs a click to get back

rules.if: you are tempted to control the mobile drawer
rules.because: the pair is a controlled DISMISSAL — there is no onSidebarOpen — so once you own the state the shell's own button can only close it

constraints: React and react-dom are the only runtime dependencies. Do not add an icon library, a router or a CSS framework to make this work.
Below 768px the sidebar becomes an overlay drawer. This is not configurable.
Nesting in navItems is capped at 3 levels; a 4th throws in development.

accessibility.keyboard: Tab reaches a skip link first, then the sidebar toggle, then top-bar actions, then the nav, then the page. Escape closes the mobile drawer and either menu. Focus entering a collapsed rail peeks it open so labels are readable.
accessibility.aria: <header> for the bar and <nav aria-label="Main"> for the sidebar. The active row carries aria-current="page" — exactly one per page. Expandable parents carry aria-expanded and an aria-controls that always resolves. The mobile drawer traps focus and restores it on close.
accessibility.notes: Expand triggers are <button>; navigation is <a>. There is never a clickable <div>. Do not add tabIndex to make a div focusable — use the right element.

propRules.rule: currentPath must be the same string form as the hrefs in navItems
propRules.why: active state is an exact match; '/orders' and '/orders/' are different pages to this component

propRules.rule: notifications and profile each render nothing when omitted
propRules.why: a profile menu with no user has nothing to draw, and a bell that opens an empty panel is an affordance that lies

composition.childrenContract: Page content. Direct children are spaced 16px apart by <main>, which is a flex column. Anything deeper should use Stack, Grid or Card — see their guards.
composition.notes: AppShell must not be nested inside another AppShell.

antiPatterns.dont: Hardcoding nav rows inside the shell or its subcomponents
antiPatterns.why: the shell derives depth, active state and the collapsed rail from the tree; a hand-written row silently opts out of all three
the shell mounts them at a fixed right-edge position; composing them yourself breaks that consistency for no gain

antiPatterns.dont: Wrapping AppShell in a scrolling container, or giving it a fixed height
antiPatterns.do: Render it at the root and let it take the viewport
antiPatterns.why: the content area is calc(100vh - top bar) with its own overflow; an outer scroller gives you two

antiPatterns.dont: Setting margins on page content to control spacing
antiPatterns.do: Use Stack, Grid and Card, or override --shell-content-gap
antiPatterns.why: <main> zeroes UA block margins so spacing cannot drift with tag choice; your margin fights a system that was already handling it

antiPatterns.dont: Patching the shell's CSS to restyle it
antiPatterns.why: class names are hashed and will change between versions; the tokens are the supported surface

antiPatterns.dont: Passing isSidebarOpen and expecting the top bar button to open the drawer
antiPatterns.do: Leave it undefined, or provide your own opening control
antiPatterns.why: the controlled pair is dismissal-only; there is no onSidebarOpen

incorrect.why: navigation belongs in navItems; a hand-written nav gets no active state, no collapse and no depth handling
use the notifications and profile props — the shell places these two itself so they stay in the same position across applications
AppShell owns the viewport and its own scroll container; an outer scroller produces two scrollbars
